verdicts.note: Raw page fetched from lareviewofbooks.org (HTTP 200). Third body paragraph (the one beginning 'This is not at all the novel I had imagined'). The sentence names all three works with dates and ends 'but he doesn't want to', and the next sentence says his style has become more spare. Both limbs supported.

verdicts.trueWording: Cultures are like people, it seems
verdicts.note: Raw LARB page. In the paragraph on libraries and archives ('The reclone of Smithe is an archive...'), Gordon quotes the narrator Smithe, 'in the literary voice of his originary writer', on books; the quoted line continues 'Sure, they get old and die; but sometimes they die even when they are not very old at all.' Attribution to Wolfe's narrator and the cultures-die-like-people sense are both on the page; 'plain aphorism' is a description of the quoted sentence's own form, not Gordon's wording.

verdicts.trueWording: a passage that evokes the style of The Book
verdicts.note: Raw LARB page, penultimate body paragraph ('That is how Wolfe portrays the "New America"...'). Gordon writes that in a few places the beautiful language of the earlier work appears briefly, then: Smithe opens a book he had written 13 years before he died to read a passage that evokes the style of The Book of the New Sun, quoting it and calling it a reminder of the Library of Ultan. All limbs supported.

verdicts.trueWording: he keeps trying new ways of writing
verdicts.note: Raw Guardian page fetched (HTTP 200). Final paragraph of the piece: 'He's my hero because he keeps trying new ways of writing and because he remains as kind and as patient with me...'. Verbatim, and in the final paragraph as cited.

verdicts.trueWording: Wolfe shifts his pacing everywhere in his stories very freely
verdicts.note: Raw Wayback capture (20201116152809id_) of nyrsf.com fetched successfully. In the paragraph beginning 'The acceleration of the slingshot ending is a matter of pacing'; the sentence continues 'creating wonderful, rhythmic effects in the flow of the telling'. Verbatim.

verdicts.trueWording: no telling if it will cover a second or a year
verdicts.note: Same raw Wayback capture, same pacing paragraph: 'Just as there is no knowing what the content of the next sentence is going to be, there is also no telling if it will cover a second or a year or stand outside time entirely.' Verbatim; the page adds the further option of standing outside time, which the claim does not contradict.

verdicts.trueWording: written entirely at the same pace, either plodding or frenetic
verdicts.note: Same raw capture, same pacing paragraph: 'What joy, after the too many volumes written entirely at the same pace, either plodding or frenetic but in any case ever so predictable and painful to one's urge to flow or bop.' Verbatim; the fault-finding and the predictability limb are both explicit.

verdicts.trueWording: one falls on Wolfe's pages as on music after a metronome
verdicts.note: Same raw capture, closing sentence of the pacing paragraph, immediately after the sentence about volumes written entirely at the same pace. Verbatim.

verdicts.trueWording: syntax, sensibility, precision, and analytical power reminiscent of Proust
verdicts.note: Same raw capture, in the Proust discussion (paragraph ending the Fifth Head / Number Five naming anecdote). Robinson describes the moment Wolfe 'spoke in a voice he would use often afterward, a characteristic Wolfe style', in which those qualities 'are set on the clones, robots, six-armed monsters, and all the rest of the matter of his beloved pulp tradition'. Verbatim; the mature-voice and pulp-material limbs are both supported.

verdicts.trueWording: stories usually are not allegories but events in themselves
verdicts.note: Same raw capture, in the allegory discussion: 'This doesn't seem to be Wolfe's method. His stories usually are not allegories but events in themselves, something like dreams or vases.' Verbatim.
